title: Proactive Shadow-Eval Pipeline for Catalog and Tenant Model Locks
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Problem: When a model version in the public catalog or a customer-pinned (tenant-locked) version is changed, we lack a lightweight, low-risk mechanism that measures end-to-end quality drift before traffic is routed. Existing preflight and canary flows are either too heavy (full canaries with real traffic) or too slow to run for frequent small catalog edits. Goal: Build a proactive 'shadow-eval' pipeline that automatically triggers when a catalog entry or tenant model lock is created/changed. The pipeline will run a focused probe suite in shadow against the new version, compute delta metrics against the incumbent, and emit a summarized verdict and recommended action. This should be non-blocking by default (does not prevent promotes), but integrated into Console signals and alerting so SRE/PM/Support get fast, prescriptive insights. Constraints: keep cost budgeted, prefer synthetic probes over real-customer traffic, avoid storing PII in eval logs, and design for tenant-aware sampling and per-tenant privacy controls.
acceptance_criteria: On catalog or tenant-lock change, a shadow eval job is scheduled automatically within 5 minutes
Shadow probe suite executes within configurable cost budget and completes within 30 minutes for 95% of runs
Delta report generated containing latency, correctness (task-specific metrics), hallucination proxy, and a composite risk score
Verdict attached to the catalog/lock object in Console with a link to detailed report and replay artifacts
Alerting rules emit to SLO/QA channels if composite risk crosses configured thresholds
Shadow runs respect tenant privacy settings and do not leak sensitive inputs to shared dashboards
success_metrics: % of catalog/lock changes with shadow eval completed within 30m >= 95%
Reduction in post-promotion quality regressions detected in orgs with evaluated locks >= 40% over baseline
Average cost per shadow eval run kept below defined cost guard (configurable)
Time-to-awareness for regression (internal alert) reduced from hours to < 20 minutes for high-risk events
design_notes: Trigger points: catalog entry create/update, tenant model lock create/update, pin upgrades from Console UI or API
Execution mode: shadow runs use synthetic probe harness with optional sampled production replay (for consenting tenants)
Isolation: run jobs in a separate non-customer-facing pool to avoid impacting latency SLOs
Scoring: produce both absolute metrics and delta against baseline; composite risk score combines quality and latency regressions weighted by customer impact
Cost controls: per-run budget, global daily budget, and abort-on-threshold to avoid runaway eval costs
Observability: summary card in Console with traffic-aware context, per-tenant drilldowns, and historical trendline
rollout_plan: MVP: implement scheduler + probe runner + minimal report UI for catalog changes in staging (2 weeks)
Pilot: enable for internal tenants and two low-risk customers; gather signal and iterate on probe set (2 weeks)
Gradual rollout: opt-in for tenants via Console toggle; default enabled for catalog-managed models after pilot
Post-launch: add sampling of real-request replay for consenting tenants and automated run-rate tuning
Fallback: if composite risk exceeds emergency threshold, flag for manual hold and create an incident-play task
